NEW: SPECIAL REPORT | Iranian Direct Action in the United States and Europe Must Be Understood Through a Framework of War, Not Terrorism

Iran is conducting a direct action campaign against US and allied targets in Europe as part of its war effort. Defining Iran’s actions as state-sponsored terrorism, while creating effective legal frameworks for prosecution and responses, obfuscates the nature of Iran’s campaign.

To read the full special report, tap the link in bio and navigate to "Publications."

Iran began its attacks in Europe in March 2026, shortly after the Iran war began, by sponsoring and supporting attacks on Jewish targets across Europe.

Many of these attacks failed, and not every planned attack was executed.

Iran is likely learning that direct action raids and the threat of raids are far more effective than terror attacks in Europe.

Both the United States and Europe must understand Iranian actions as part of a broader military campaign, not as “terrorism” or other criminal frameworks.

Russian Offensive Campaign Assessment, November 13, 2026: The United States and Ukraine continue to view the involvement of European officials in future peace negotiations with Russia as necessary. Moscow, however, is willing to let European officials participate in talks only about a new European security architecture – not about resolving the war in Ukraine – and continues to insist that Europe concede fully to Russia’s original 2021 demand to dismantle NATO.

To read the report, go to the link in our bio, and select "Publications."

Other Key Takeaways:
Kremlin officials are accepting the idea of European participation in future peace negotiations only as they relate to Russian efforts to dismantle the post-Cold War security architecture in Europe.

Russian officials continue to call for a humanitarian mission in Kostyantynivka, Donetsk Oblast, based on the false parallelism between Kostyantynivka and occupied Oleshky, Kherson Oblast, that the Kremlin is trying to construct.

A ceasefire, like the one in Oleshky, is impossible to execute in Kostyantynivka, however, because the actual frontline military situations are not comparable.

ISW continues to assess that the Kremlin is very likely seeking to use a temporary localized ceasefire in Kostyantynivka to set conditions for a military build-up in the area needed to drive northward to Druzhkivka, one of Ukraine’s most heavily fortified cities on the Fortress Belt defense line.

Ukrainian officials continue to report disruptions in SpaceX’s Starshield satellite communications services that are significantly hindering Ukraine’s ability to intercept Russian drones and conduct its intermediate-range strike campaign in occupied Ukraine, despite SpaceX denials.

Russia is using seized assets of Western companies operating in Russia to fund its war in Ukraine.

An improvised explosive device (IED) detonated in Moscow City on November 13 and injured a former advisor to former pro-Russian Ukrainian Prime Minister Mykola Azarov.

Ukrainian forces recently advanced east of Slovyansk and south of Novopavlivka.

Russia launched 117 drones against Ukraine overnight.

Iran Update, November 13, 2026: Increased cooperation among Yemeni government-aligned forces likely enabled these forces to successfully halt a Houthi offensive operation and recapture territory in southeastern Lahij Governorate. The threat the Houthi advance poses to southern Yemeni territory likely motivated some Southern Transitional Council (STC)-aligned factions to increase their cooperation and coordination with forces currently fighting the Houthis in the area.

To read the full update, go to the link in bio, and select "Publications."

Other Key Takeaways:
Saudi aircraft simultaneously provided close air support to aid the Yemeni government-aligned forces’ counterattack by targeting Houthi frontline units in Madaribah wa al Arah District and Houthi logistics necessary to sustain Houthi operations in the area. Saudi aircraft targeted Houthi forces and materiel in al Turbah, southern Taiz Governorate, a key staging area for the Houthis that is located about 30 kilometers north of al Majza.

The Iraqi federal government began a highly circumscribed investigation into Kataib Hezbollah’s involvement in oil smuggling in Jurf al Sakhr, Babil Province, on November 13. An Iraqi federal government investigation committee conducted a field inspection of Kataib Hezbollah’s Jurf al Sakhr stronghold on November 13, according to multiple Iraqi media reports and footage from the area.

Iraqi Prime Minister Ali al Zaydi almost certainly made a deal with Iranian-backed Iraqi actors to allow an investigation of this nature as a balance between efforts to hold Iranian-backed Iraqi militias accountable and to avoid armed conflict with Kataib Hezbollah. This investigation, which appears to be highly coordinated with the militias, follows a previous attempt by the government to enter Jurf al Sakhr without militia permission.

Iran Update, November 14, 2026: The Houthis launched ballistic missiles targeting Yemeni government-aligned forces’ military staging areas and weapons depots in Lahij and Aden governorates, likely to disrupt logistics that support Yemeni government forces in southeastern Lahij Governorate.

To read the full update, tap the link in bio and navigate to "Publications."

Other Key Takeaways:

Yemeni government-aligned forces have continued to recapture territory and advance in southeastern Lahij Governorate despite the Houthi attacks on logistics infrastructure, however.

Saudi aircraft continued to provide close air support to aid Yemeni government-aligned forces’ counterattacks by targeting Houthi frontline units in Madaribah wa al Arah District and Houthi logistics necessary to sustain Houthi operations in the area.

Iranian naval forces continue to claim that commercial vessels are striking naval mines along the US-backed route in the southern part of the Strait of Hormuz, likely to undermine ship operators’ confidence in US escort operations and compel vessels to transit through Iranian territorial waters.

Russian Offensive Campaign Assessment, November 14, 2026: US proposals for Ukraine’s possible NATO membership are implicit rejections of Russian demands to stop NATO expansion and reform the European security architecture.

To read the full update, tap the link in bio and navigate to "Publications."

Other Key Takeaways:

Moscow not only remains committed to its original 2021 ultimatums to the United States and NATO but is also reportedly expanding its demands in order to completely dismantle the post-Cold War security architecture in Europe.

Russian President Vladimir Putin is committed to his original war aim of destroying NATO in order to reassert Russia’s control over its perceived sphere of influence in Europe and beyond.

The United States continues to call for the inclusion of European delegations in upcoming multilateral negotiations on the war in Ukraine.

The temporary localized ceasefire in Kostyantynivka that the Kremlin is requesting would likely facilitate Russia’s reinforcement of the southern flank of the Fortress Belt — allowing Russian forces to set conditions for renewed efforts to seize Kostyantynivka and Dobropillya.

Recent Russian mechanized assaults and the relatively high tempo of Russian attacks in the Kostyantynivka and Dobropillya directions on the southern flank of Ukraine’s Fortress Belt demonstrate the Russian military command’s prioritization of this sector of the frontline.

Ukrainian officials reported the sixth day of speed restrictions on SpaceX’s Starshield satellite network over parts of Ukraine, inhibiting Ukraine’s ability to effectively defend against the jet-powered drones that Russian forces launch from occupied Ukraine.

Russian forces recently advanced northeast of Lyman, and east of Slovyansk. Ukrainian forces recently advanced south of Novopavlivka and east of Oleksandrivka.

Russia launched 96 drones at Ukraine overnight.
